author: m0_ox
content:
To be very clear here, I agree that the process is ambiguous at the moment and needs to be sharpened. I think there are some parallel friction points here wrt specs especially. One is that CFI'd EIPs being included in devnets are being chosen by very few people at times and forced into implementation. And another is that the specs (consensus) seems to merge into the main spec these CFI EIPs rather than only merge SFI EIPs into main spec.

Correct me if I'm wrong on the consensus-specs side.

> To me it is a no brainer that we must not merge into that next-fork-branch EIPs that are not SFId and EIPs that clients aren't forced to implement.

On the execution-specs we don't merge anything that isn't SFI into the main spec. Each CFI EIP is implemented standalone on an `eips/bogota/eip-NNNN` branch and we have a github workflow that merges EIP branches together to create a devnet branch (`devnets/heze/3`, for example) – with humans sussing out any conflicts where EIPs interact. From this devnet branch we cut the test release for the devnets.

So I think there is some disconnect between "something is CFI'd and we need to test it so it goes in this devnet" and "merging this spec into the actual fork".
